title: Kansas City Chiefs vs Seattle Seahawks - Official Postgame Show | Chiefs Rewind
text: [music] under pressure. BACK AT THE 31 YD LINE. NOW THROWS a wheel out right side. IT'S CAUGHT. [music] TOUCHDOWN AT THE FAR front pylon. Herbert is absolutely eaten alive. It's Drew The pass is going to be OH MY GOODNESS. WHAT A CATCH BY TAQUAN THORNTON. Here comes a rush and he's GOING TO GO DOWN. GEORGE CARLOS. WELL, the undefeated season uh comes to an end. The Chiefs dropped to 5-1 here by losing to the Seattle Seahawks by a score of 20 to3. A team that has been so good on prime time here at home since 2010. But this game really the Seahawks felt like they had control of this game really wire to wire. >> Well, you know, we ran into a team tonight in Seattle that was fighting for their season. They're three and three. They cannot afford to fall to three and four. They're in prime time. They're the defending champs. And we turned in our worst game of the year early in all three phases. one of those things that we have to learn from and turn the page pretty quickly. >> Yeah. And yet in San Francisco lost. So Seattle thinks they can get back within two games, which they did. All right. There's some things here though. Offensively, there was an opportunity. The first three possessions of the game, the Chiefs got into Seattle territory uh and a play that would have been first and 10 with K9 in a pass play down to the 30 yd line of Sandal gets wiped out on a legal shift penalty on Travis Kelce. That's one. Two. Uh uh third down and four at the 42 of Seattle. Incomplete. There's two. No points. Three. Patrick throws an interception uh at the 33 of Seattle. If you get threes on those, you're at nine points and it could change even the u the psychology of this game dramatically. >> We'll allow one more. How about in the third quarter? We had the offsetting penalties that wiped out the great catch by K9. Uh this was a game that came down to the margins once again. So, the scoreboard doesn't show it, but we talked about the importance of the margins in this game on a field pass really all week long. And we lost consistently in the margins here tonight. Whether it be the plays that you talked about, the two missed field goals, the interception, uh the tackling defensively was really disappointing here tonight because the Chiefs have been the best team in the NFL in terms of not missing tackles. We missed a ton of tackles here tonight. And really, the story of the game is the struggles on third and long all night long. We can talk about it more, but third and nine, third and 10, we have to get off the field and consistently Seattle's moving the chains on those plays. >> Yeah, let's jump in there right now because this last year was an issue in the second half of the season, but Seattle tonight converted. Third and nine, third and nine. Third and nine, third and nine, third and 10. Two were Darnold scrambles. Another one's a checkown throw. To your point on the missed tackles, I don't think they're even trying to think they're going to get a first down on that play. They do get a double- digit play. If you get a stop on just again, you just changed the game dramatic. If you get a stop on two of those third down and longs. >> Yeah. Overall, Seattle goes 11 of 16 on third down. Very difficult to win in the NFL if you're allowing the opponent to convert 11 of 16 at third down opportunities. Seven of them were third and six or longer. Five of them were third and nine or longer. Third and nine, you have to get off the field. This defense has been so good this year. It's the number two scoring defense in the NFL coming into this game. top five in so many categories. That's not the performance that we expected here tonight. They're better than they showed here tonight. >> Yeah, the Chief Stall to 5- one. The Seahawks go to four and three. Are kind of back in it now in the rough and tumble NFC West. Well, let's get some reaction from the podium from Coach Reed and also from Patrick Mahomes. >> All right. Uh really not uh anything injury-wise to mention. Nick uh had some spasms in his neck and he'll work through that and be good. Listen, all um all three phases uh we struggled in. So, we've got to do better uh as a and that's my responsibility. So, I take full responsibility for this. Uh we've got to we've got to play better as a team, a tough place to play, but this is all part of it. They're a good football team and they they played well. My hat goes off to them. Uh there's not a whole lot of stats that I can share with you that really make any sense. Maybe other than third downs both sides of the ball. We we can do a better job uh with those, but we've got a great locker room here and the guys will get back in and get themselves ready to play against a good Denver team uh this next week. So with that, time's yours. [clears throat] >> What enabled them to sort of stifle the run and the pass? That that's because you guys present a lot of complications for most teams. >> Yeah, I'll take responsibility for that. putting guys in the right position to to make plays. Um so, you know, they they they did they did a great job both both areas and um you know, we'll get better at it. We just got to go back to the drawing board here a little bit. >> I know I know you've had faith in Harrison, but it looked like he left one short, which is a little uncharacteristic of him. Is anything going wrong physically or >> All three all three phases with the with everybody had their, you know, had had an issue starting with me. So, it's uh we all had a piece of that. >> Andy, how much did the the pressure disrupt what you were trying to do offensively? >> Yeah. I mean, they they did a good job uh defensively. I mean, they they had pressure. Um so, we can do better better versus that. We um [clears throat] again, some of it's play calls and we'll take care of that. >> Follow up on Harrison. What's your concern level with him right now? >> Yeah, I mean, listen, he's been one of the most consistent kickers in uh football, but um he's off a bit, so got to fix it. >> Andy, defensively, what there were a lot of like between third and five and third and 10. Did you obviously you saw the common denominator, you fixed it, but what what what stuck out to you about how we >> Yeah, you got to keep yourself especially against this this group here. You got to keep yourself out of third and long situations and thus you got to do better on first and second down. So, we we can we can do better. We had some penalties in there also that kind of got us going the wrong direction um when we were moving the ball and you got to take care of those. any particular message you leave the team with after game like this? >> Yeah, we got to learn from it. I you I mentioned to you guys before, win or lose, you got to learn and get better and so uh and we'll all do that. I'll start with myself and >> [clears throat] >> uh we'll work our way through it and make sure that we we teach and u and you got to have the right locker room to handle that. and I' I feel like I've got a a great locker room. So, uh that they'll take care of business here. >> Any wonder if you could comment on anything on the Josh Simmons report about meeting at all. >> Yeah, listen Sam, I I've I've said so much on him. Rick's talked about him this and that. Things happen and uh that's no that's no reason that it uh he was put on IR. he's got a bad back and so um he's got to get that worked [clears throat] out and that's uh the main thing but um that's I'll leave it at that. I mean that's where we're at with it. >> All right. >> Yeah, I mean got your got your tail kicked. Um didn't execute um offensively especially um especially around that midfield area. um kept us away from a lot of points um or at least enough points to be competitive. Um but it's stuff you got to learn from. I mean that's obviously a really good defense and u we didn't execute at a high enough level to have success. >> One of the things you guys have been able to do is present enough options to make it difficult for a team to stop at all, but it seemed like they were pretty effective on all aspects of the game. >> Yeah, they did a great job. You know, they they they passed off their zones. They played man when they needed to play man. Um and then they got us off the field on third down. um uh we moved the ball a little bit kind of in between like where you get it from kickoff to the midfield, but in order to have success in this league, you got to be able to sustain drives and we weren't weren't able to do that and um obviously they contain the explosive plays. So, it's uh um stuff that we have to continue to get better at. Um and you can't have those mistakes versus defense. >> How much did their pressure really affect what you guys wanted to do? Yeah, I mean obviously a little bit, but uh I thought especially early in the game, I thought my feet were were kind of getting me into trouble where I could have maybe sat in the pocket um and made some of the throws down the field. Um I got better a little bit later in the game. Um but at the same time, whenever you play a team like that, um you can't let them get ahead and kind of get into a game they want to play. Um because obviously they've had a lot of success doing that. And so um you got to be better starting faster. Um especially with me um and then uh try to do better throughout the entire game. What did you see just on the interception there? >> Yeah, I mean obviously he was trying to make the throw. Um kind of really had two guys in the area, but I was really trying to throw it to 11. Um got kind of pulled down as I was throwing it and it settled high over the top of his head. Um you don't want to put the ball in harm's way, especially in that midfield area, I believe on second down. So just just trying to find a way to get either get the ball to him and make a a throw um or throw the ball away. So I got to be better there. >> Go ahead. Well, what what's what's the takeaway you want the guys to have from this game? [snorts] >> Yeah, I mean, I think the biggest takeaway is if you don't come ready to play, it's just you can get your tail kicked in this league and no matter if you're five and0 or whatever it is, like it's every week's a new week and um every team can do this and so you have to have that mindset of of when you go throughout the week of practice of we need our best football that Sunday and um I have to do the same as well. And so, we got a young team. Um it'll be about how we respond from this obviously with a big game coming up this next week. So, let's get let's get rolling and and get ourselves ready for that. Is >> this something you're saying based on just moving forward or something you're saying based on reflecting on the last week? >> No, I think it was just moving forward, you know. Um, you never know. I mean, we've we've played in some prime time games, but they all can go so many different ways. And so, um, like I said, as a young team, it's a learning experience. Um, but for us veteran guys, we got to show them how we respond from this. I think that that'll be the biggest thing is that, um, just like how this game went, we can go out there and play better the next week. It in this league, it's week to week. Um, and it's about going out there and having a great week of practice and uh, getting oursel prepared for another great defense. >> This is a little bit related, Patrick, but you had a little bit of a history of, you know, when you've had a game like this, like surging kind of afterwards. What in your mind, what's the key to that transformation? And >> I mean, same things you said. >> I think I think the biggest thing is like you I mean, you got to feel it. I mean, this is this sucks. You don't you don't want to perform like this in prime time. Um, on a big big moment like this. Um, so you got to feel it on that plane ride home and and understand that it sucks, but then how how can you build off of it? Like that that's the biggest thing is, um, as we get back and and get get back to that film study on the Broncos, you have to see where you made your mistakes and how they're going to try to execute and then do stuff to combat that and play better. And so um, obviously it sucks right now. Um, but we'll be we'll be full steam ahead trying to do our our best to to find a way to win this next week. and we've seen K9 be such a difference maker for you guys, but from your perspective, what did they do to really lock down the running game? >> Yeah, I mean, we have to help him. I think that's the biggest thing is when they put so many eggs in that in that basket of stopping the run game, we have to have the play action game and the movement game to be able to to throw the ball. Um, and if we're not proving that, they're going to continue to put those put those guys up at the line of scrimmage and and that that's hard for the run game. And he made the most of with the opportunities that he had. But for me, having some of those play actions early in the game, if I can hit some of those, um, it'll loosen up the defense and then he can kind of get going. And that's what we've been so good at this year. And obviously, we didn't do it this year, uh, this game. >> Patrick, pre- snap, it looked like you were doing a lot, moving people around, trying to get people in the right spot. Was that a crowd noise thing, or was that just maybe guys just not being on the right right page at the right time? Yeah, I mean just like I said, it's a young team and just trying to communicate and make sure everybody's on the same page and we made our mistakes here and there, but I thought I was proud of how the guys fought at the end um in that second half. Obviously, we didn't play and score touchdowns, but guys were were fighting to make plays happen and so we'll learn from this um and we we'll be better from it. >> Okay, thanks. >> Done better defensively. >> It's a lot of things we could have done better. I think we gave up a 21 yardd run. um a few more stops on third down that we we let slip on us. Um I think more so just watching the film and u being critical of yourself um as a player as an individual then also as a whole as a defense as a whole or offense as a whole. >> How difficult is it to to bring down Sam? I I know he's did [clears throat] in the pocket and you know you had a couple chances with him escaping. I guess just how how much of a challenge was that end up being tonight? I think we got to do a better job as a Dline as in um closing the pocket um filling those voids to making sure he's he doesn't have a skate lane. I think we didn't do such a good job today because he was able to make a third down once again a positive yard game. So I think that's something we can look at film and we can correct. Um just watching Phil more so watch film correct the error is what we made and get ready and prepare for Denver. Anybody else? >> Chris, any particular message for the young guys, offense, defense? Any any message going forward after this one? >> Um, like the it's just like a little adversity in life. You know, you're going to face adversity some point in time in life. You know, we all have aspirations of want to go undefeated. You know, that's always the goal. And sometimes you face adversity. And you know, it's a point in time you going to face it, but it's about how you how how you come back cuz you're going to face it at some point in time. It's some some area in your life. Adversity is going to hit you. It's about how you bounce back. So, I think we got the guys on this team um with with a lot of high character that we've been in this situation before. Um you know, you go back to last year and then you we fast forward to where we are now. We're sitting five and one. It's a lot of good going into that, but you know, for us, I think it's more specific. Um, correcting our errors and being prepared for for Denver coming up. >> What What's Coach Reed's message after after a game like this in the locker room and and how do you guys move forward, you know, from that? >> Just correct the errors in all phase of the game. I think this was a game where we um [clears throat] we we we struggle in all phases as a as a team. as a team, special teams, offense, defense, it's not no one particular area. And I think we can bounce back as a team also. You know, have a great week of practice. Preparation is always key. And look forward for the upcoming opponent. >> Thank you. >> So disappointment there and Patrick obviously disappointed. In fact, you brought up the point um this is the third worst defeat of Patrick's career. He doesn't get beat 20 to3 very much. Patrick Mahomes has played 132 career regular season games. He's lost by more than eight points just six times now. Think about that. It puts things in perspective. Games like this don't happen very often. That's why when it happens, we're like, "What happened?" Because during Patrick Mahomes career, we don't lose by more than a touchdown, if we lose at all. It happens every once in a while. One thing that makes Patrick and this team so special though is they learn from these things. They don't let these things snowball. That's the challenge here this week. Noah Williams made a big play at the end of the second quarter. Seahawks are up 10 to nothing. Could have been 17. They're at the 2yd line, but he gets an interception and runs it past the 50 yd line. Not only stopping Seattle from scoring, but giving the Chiefs a chance to score at the end of the half. It was a big play for Null, his first career interception. >> Awesome play. He almost scored on that play. It was nearly a 14-point swing. But that gets back to the margins of this game where whenever something positive happened, something negative would happen soon after. So, we have that huge play in the end zone. Everyone's feeling good. And if you hit that field goal going into halftime, we have all the momentum going into half despite not playing very well, but you miss that field goal. Kind of makes you feel not so great about the interception. It's a great play for null and our red zone defense there, but we got to hit that field goal on the back end. >> Yeah. And then also some records tonight for Kel. Uh not a big night, 44 yards, but he did have three receptions. He now is number five all time of any player in NFL history on the number of receptions. Another one he made on that same play is when you count his uh regular season and postseason, uh he now has the most receiving yards of any tight end in NFL history. >> That's amazing. I know he'd be the first though to say he doesn't care at all right now and just wants to win the football game. But it is pretty incredible. And despite a tough night here in this one, we got to appreciate Travis Kelce because the guy makes history every single week. But again, I think if you told him next week you're going to catch one pass for one yard, but we beat the Broncos, he'd take that. >> So now the transition goes to playing the Broncos next Sunday afternoon. Uh the Broncos able to win today against the Arizona Cardinals. Now the Chiefs out of the ranks of the unbeatens. By the way, if you had on your bingo card the last remaining undefeated team going into week eight with the Minnesota Vikings winning every game like 1413, then uh bingo for you. Right now though, the Chiefs tied still with Buffalo for the best record in the AFC. >> Yeah, that's a positive right there. So, we gave ourselves some room for error this season by having the 5-0 start. That was the issue with last year is we are constantly digging out of a hole. But like I always talk about when we lose on Rewind, we can't let this snowball into more losses. And a huge game next week against the Broncos. It's only what, week eight, but as far as week eight games go, it's pretty important because if we can win that game, we have the head-to-head tiebreaker over Denver the rest of the year as we're trying to get back and win this division. Huge game next week. We got to clean up a lot of the things that we struggled at here tonight. Whether it be the long third downs, allowing Jackson Smith and Jigba to have a huge game, can't let the receivers have a big game next week. A lot to clean up, but we have the guys that can do it. >> And hopefully Rashi Rice back next week. Chiefs lose it 20-3 uh here to the Seattle Seahawks and now get ready for the Denver Broncos in a big game. Try chance to sweep the Broncos before Veterans Day or Voting Day. That'll be next week. For Matt McMullen, I'm Mitch Holtus. Thanks for joining us on this edition of Chiefs Rewind. Chiefs Rewind is brought to you by Ford, the official car and truck of the Kansas City Chiefs, and by Community America Credit Union, the official banking partner of the Kansas City Chiefs.

title: Kellen Moore Recaps Saints' Loss to Steelers in Paris
text: OK.  OK.  I would like to first say how grateful we are to everyone in France, Paris, Versailles—everyone who helped organize this event.  I think it was a great event and a very good game today. Of course, unfortunately, we didn't win, and that's very disappointing.  We had opportunities, but in the end, our opponent had several successful game episodes.  In this game, everything is decided by little things, and when moments arise, you have to take advantage of them, and they took advantage of them better than us. How do you plan to improve your takeaway game? We have a week off now , and we have to put in a lot of effort because, again , there is too much instability. There are weeks when everything is fine, and there are weeks when it's not.  Today we failed to create any movement or breakthrough during the away games.  17 of 18. Tyler made a few runs, but, you know, it wasn't enough.  We had to throw the ball a lot, and we have to fix that. Are you ready for changes in the lineup? We just need to seriously work on it and figure it out. Again, when the week off rolls around, we go into evaluation mode to identify issues that need to be worked on and address them. Do you already have a plan for staff changes? We need to evaluate everything.  I'm not going to make any hasty decisions right now. get better, and that's what we'll focus on . Do you already feel like you understand what exactly needs to be changed in the ball handling? I think we need to really dig into this from the beginning, evaluate the entire season as a whole, and find a solution. So, the main focus this weekend will be on ball removal, right? Of course, this is an important part of our work. When you have a day like today—17 carries for 18 yards—it's going to be hard to win games playing like that.  So , you know, even though there were other moments that I think were really positive for our team, we couldn't pull it off You mentioned disappointment. Yes.    Is this the main reason or was there something else? I think the thing is that in small details.  When you look at third downs, the red zone, their ability to carry the ball and create three-and-three, three-and-four or two-and- two situations, they continue to use the carry effectively in those moments.  They were just able to continue their drives.  It was a game where possession was limited .  You have to appreciate every moment with the ball. Now, when a kicker misses at least one kick or punt in six out of seven games. I think it's fair to say that we have to evaluate it.  And go through this process during the week off.    Do you think the late arrival this week had an impact? I wouldn't say so.  Eventually , another team arrived at the same time as us.  So no. What is your level of concern about what seemed like there were a lot of......pretty consistent slow starts throughout the games and issues stopping the carry.  Does it bother you that the same problems arise every week? Yes, it's always disappointing.  Again , we have to play better away from home .  We can't afford to have a week like last week, when we were happy with ourselves, and then find ourselves in a situation like today.  So, again , this causes a lot of frustration.    Do you feel there is a solution?  What will you be able to find them? Yes.  I think there is definitely a possibility to find these solutions.  We need to understand this more deeply We have to analyze everything. You need to put emotions aside. title: This actually WORKS for the 49ers…
text: I just stepped out of the 49ers locker room here in Atlanta. And I have to say that four years ago on this very same spectacular field, the 49ers lost a similar game to the Falcons and and I just talked to Kyle Yuschek. He said the same thing. This felt a lot like the 2022 loss. Too many giveaways, not enough pass rush, and that allowed Atlanta to have a bunch of easy passes. And in this game in particular, the 49ers special teams was a disaster. A complimentary loss for a team that is now 6-1. But we cannot forget what happened four years ago after they lost here. The 49ers just days later traded for Christian McAffrey. Then they got a bunch of injured guys back. They didn't have Nick Bosa for the loss here in Atlanta in 2022. They will have Nick Bosa coming out of the by-week. And they went on a run. That's what the 49ers are going to be focused on next. But today, I mean, I think Fred Warner summarizes this one well. >> I'm a believer on the road, you always have to pack your defense. Pack your defense, you pack your special teams, right? I felt like we were ready for the challenge to come out and play our best game, and unfortunately, we just didn't do that. I felt like we had so many opportunities to take the ball away. Um, I was super close on a couple of those punch outs, and it just the the ball just didn't happen to fall on the ground, right? And so, um, it's no excuse at the end of the day. Uh it is what it is, right? They outplayed us and so we got to make sure we go back, we look at it hard, correct the mistakes and uh get ready for the next round. >> The 49ers most definitely did not pack their defense for the vast majority of this game. And that special teams, it is a concern. Kyle Shanahan did not directly answer the question about whether the 49ers would bring in competition for Eddie Pierro after his fourth missed extra point of the season. Uh, I don't know. I haven't talked to anybody about that. We'll probably discuss on the plane. >> And the special teams woes go back to the opening kickoff return for Atlanta. Over 60 yards. And that gave the Falcons some life right after Christian McCaffrey hopped over the goal line to give the 49ers an early 7 nothing lead. I think early in this game, the 49ers were winning the arm wrestling match in a way that they expected to win it because they knew that they were better than the Falcons, even down so many wide receivers. But special teams opened the door for Atlanta and then of course the Kalon Black fumble further opened the door for the Falcons. From that point, from the fumble all the way until the 49ers were on a desperation drive down 12 points and Brock Perie hit Jordan Watkins on a big gainer. Atlanta ran 36 plays and the 49ers only ran seven. That 2022 game, Atlanta just possessed the football. They controlled the ground game and they possessed the football in this one. They they possessed the football for that big stretch without really rushing all too effectively. The 49ers, I wouldn't say they shut down Bejan Robinson, but they held him to 2.8 yards per carry, but they just could not get off the field. They only hit pressure on three of 34 Michael Penn Jr. drop packs today, but he didn't throw a ball more than 10 yards downfield until the second half. Well, the player who doesn't normally play for the 49ers who was in there was Jack Jones today. Their essentially their fourth quarterback. Upton Stout didn't end up playing. So Jones was the weakness that the Falcons picked on and they converted like four first downs just working against Jones. Like did I go in that game with we had four active receivers, which I don't know if we've ever done that in the Kyle Shanahan era. Like we usually have five. Sure it's incredibly different. Like there's no Debo on the sideline over there. Like there's no wide receiver taking running back snaps. Um and there's no like Mike Evans is one of the most unique wide receivers I've ever played with. So like yes, is the game plan different? Sure. But like what I was saying earlier is like Kyle and our Kubak do a really good job of they build the offense around what we have available and then they try to put those guys in position to succeed. What you saw with Jordan Watkins today. Brandon Cooks made some good catches for us. So like we can still win with it. It's just going to look different. text: Uh oh.
